title: Per-repo sandbox definition in .tick/config.md
description:
The operator wants each repo to declare its own sandbox. This completes the image story: the batteries-included base covers the common set, and a repo that needs more says so in tracked config rather than forcing a factory-wide image rebuild.

Add a Sandbox section to .tick/config.md, the established runner-neutral contract for dispatched implementers:
- image: optional custom image reference. Absent means the version-pinned base image — the 99% path declares nothing.
- toolchain: extra tools to provision through the version manager already shipped in the base (e.g. rust 1.x), resolved on first run into the project persistent sandbox and warm thereafter.
- setup: idempotent, cache-populating commands run once per sandbox (pnpm install --frozen-lockfile in cloud/factory, go mod download). This closes a gap named twice during Phase 0: the existing Environment section is VERIFICATION only (test, do not ask) and cannot express provisioning.

SECURITY BOUNDARY, and the reason this belongs in tracked config rather than anywhere else: setup runs arbitrary shell inside a sandbox holding credentials. It must come only from the tracked, PR-reviewed repo config on the submitted SHA — never from a tick note, a model, a signal payload, or an API parameter. Same rule the design doc applies to webhook sources: adding capability is a PR, not a dashboard click.

Local runs read the same section, so a herdr worker warms identically — this must not become cloud-only config.

Consider (do not assume): a repo may already carry devcontainer.json declaring much of this. Reading it as an import path is worth evaluating, but a partial implementation of a large spec is worse than a small explicit section — if you support it, state exactly which keys are honoured and ignore the rest loudly.
acceptance_criteria: A repo with no Sandbox section runs on the base image unchanged; a repo declaring extra toolchain gets it provisioned on first run and cached after; setup commands run once per sandbox and are idempotent on re-run; setup is read only from the tracked config at the submitted SHA, proven by a test that a tick note or API parameter cannot inject a command; the same section warms a local herdr worker.
